label: The twenty years Colonel Ross has been on the turf
quote: I have been on the turf for twenty years
note: The Colonel's own claim; it runs up to the day of the race.

label: When the favourite was sent over to the race just as Holmes found him
quote: took the liberty of running him just as he was sent over
note: Holmes says he found the horse 'in the hands of a faker'. This links back to Brown's 'Should I change it first or not?' (¶140). The text does not date it, but it comes before the race.

label: When Colonel Ross scratched his other horse
quote: We scratched our other one, and put all hopes on your word
note: This was done on Holmes's word that the horse would start (¶161). It comes before the race and is not otherwise dated.

label: The day before the race, the betting at fifteen to one
quote: You could have got fifteen to one yesterday
note: After this the price shortens until it is under three to one on the race day.

label: Four days later, in the train to Winchester
quote: Four days later Holmes and I were again in the train, bound for Winchester

label: Four days later, Colonel Ross meets them outside the station at Winchester
quote: Colonel Ross met us by appointment outside the station

label: Four days later, driving in the Colonel's drag to the course
quote: we drove in his drag to the course beyond the town
note: The talk of the horse and the betting (¶184–189).

label: Four days later, the drag draws up in the enclosure near the grand stand
quote: As the drag drew up in the enclosure near the grand stand
note: Watson reads the card. The ring's cries and the numbers go up (¶190–196).

label: Four days later, a bay horse in the Colonel's colours canters past
quote: a powerful bay horse swept out from the weighing enclosure and cantered past us

labels.label: Next Tuesday, at the fall of the flag
Four days later, the start of the Wessex Cup

note: The Wessex Cup. Holmes watches the start through Watson's field-glass (¶199).

label: Four days later, the horses come up the straight and pass the post
quote: passed the post a good six lengths before its rival

label: Four days later, in the weighing enclosure with the winner
quote: as we made our way into the weighing enclosure
note: Holmes says the horse is the favourite and names the horse as Straker's killer (¶202–214).

label: Four days later, the bell for the next race
A more fitting time, for Holmes's full explanation
quote: I shall defer a lengthy explanation until a more fitting time
note: This is planned. The next race, on which Holmes has a bet, comes in between.
